proposals.evidence: DEDR3805 gives Tamil/Malayalam pakal day/daytime, Kannada pagal, Kodagu pōlï and Gondi pīal/piyāl/payal. Selected survey pakal/pagal/pahal and contracted pol/pīal-type forms retain those developments, with source vowels preserved. Generic day elicitation is kept distinct from the article’s daylight sense. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3656 explicitly gives Tamil nāḷai/nāḷaikku, Malayalam nāḷa, Kannada nāḷe, Kodagu nāḷe/nāḷēkï, Gondi nāṛ(i) and Kurux nelā tomorrow. Selected survey forms preserve the day-stem temporal/locative endings, including nāḷɛykɨ and regional vowel/lateral variants; these are ordinary inflected temporal forms. Opaque contractions and multiword temporal responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5276 explicitly gives Tamil valiya strong/big, Malayalam valiya great, Kannada bal(u)/bolu bigness and Kodagu ballyë great. These southern survey valiya/baliya/belliya-type big adjectives extend that documented family, retaining ordinary adjective endings and source vowel/length notation. The right-hand sense of the current parent is only one sense: its primary article directly supports bigness. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
